title: Fed vortices with heredity and selection (SIDH): a label carried in each vortex's own trapped fluid passes through vortex fission, a trait-blind mutation makes a new kind during the run, and the kind with 20% more gain per unit fuel rises from 0 to 0.86-0.93 of the vortices on 3/3 seeds against 0.38-0.60 in the identical-draw neutral twin
summary: world.py is the fed-vortex world (20261027T0712-c53-fed-vortex-claim, defaults unchanged) plus two labels a, b advected by the flow, copied only where the vortex eats (kl (eat/Y) a (1-a-b)), decaying at dl 0.05 elsewhere (Dl 0.02). At t=300 every eating vortex is labelled a; every 50 t one uniform draw picks an eating pixel and a and b are swapped in a 6-px disk there (the draw never reads a label, and its sequence depends only on mut_seed, so the eps 0 twin receives the same draws); kind b's gain is k (1 + eps b), so kind a keeps the base world's gain. heredity.py (c49's heredity2.py adapted: labkit segmentation and tracker on |omega| every 3 t, K=20 frames) on seeds 1-3, T=4500: with eps 0.2 the mean share of kind-b vortices over t=2000-4500 is 0.86/0.93/0.86, in the eps 0 twin 0.38/0.44/0.60 (share_b.png); births by kind b:a 189:32, 187:38, 178:40 against 34:59, 47:97, 73:47; daughters keep the parent's kind at 614/664 splits (favoured) and 297/357 (neutral). labkit packs (seeds 1, 2): 118/117 persistent splits, generation 21/19 (favoured); 54/77, generation 10/14 (neutral); merge/split 0.89-0.91 in both.

claims.statement: In pack_sel (WORLD_P eps 0.2, mut_dt 50; seeds 1 and 2) and in heredity.py runs of seeds 1-3, vortices formed from random vorticity all start as kind a at t=300; trait-blind mutations create kind-b vortices, which pass their kind through fission (daughters keep the parent's kind at 614/664 splits) and, because they gain 20% more vorticity per unit fuel, out-divide kind a (births b:a 554:110) and take 0.86-0.93 of the vortices, against 0.38-0.60 in the eps 0 twin with the same mutation draws (births b:a 154:203).
claims.track: seed 1 (pack_sel/seed1), labkit track 1597 (findtrack_s1.txt): a kind-b vortex (rendered label share a/(a+b) 0.31) born at t=4110 by a persistent split of the kind-b vortex 1575, which divides at t=4176 into the kind-b vortices 1626 and 1627, at generation 19 of the lineage (pack_sel/seed1/lineage.png)

controls_run.H: pack_neutral/ (eps 0, same seeds and mutation draw sequence, seeds 1 2) and m_s*_e0.json (heredity.py, seeds 1-3): the identical-draw neutral twin; per-kind births, mutation-linked flips and off-kind daughters in m_s*_e*.json, heredity_summary.txt
controls_run.D: pack_dthalf and pack_noadv of the parent world (20261027T0712-c53-fed-vortex-claim)

claims.bd_control: Not rerun for the labelled world; the parent world's no-advection twin loses ongoing division (20261027T0712-c53-fed-vortex-claim/pack_noadv).

limits: Vortices are label mixtures: median purity 0.58-0.73 (p10 ~0.51), because a 6-px mutation disk converts only part of a vortex and a/b vortices fuse; kinds are majority labels, and 8-12% of daughters fall on the other side of 0.5 from their parent (50/664 favoured, 60/357 neutral). Kind flips of living vortices away from a logged mutation: 17, 11, 15 (favoured) and 0, 11, 8 (neutral) against 31-40 at mutations; these are probably fusions with other-kind vortices and partial mutations, and are reported, not removed. The fitness effect is written (the label scales the gain), mutation is frequent (84 per run) and symmetric, so the neutral twin drifts toward 0.5. Higher gain also changes the population: kind-b vortices are larger and more elongated and divide about twice as often (persistent splits 221/225/218 vs 93/144/120 in heredity.py), which is the selection. Deaths are mostly fusions, which heredity.py does not count as deaths, so only births per kind are informative. The twin receives the same draw sequence, but each draw picks an eating pixel of its own state, so targets differ between arms after the first. E not claimed for the labelled world. 128^2, T=4500, one parameter point; no dt/2 or grid test of the labelled world.
